candidates.claim: The detail route's loader already fetches the network via getById, and RouteComponent then fetches the same network again with trpcReact getById.useQuery. The loader only uses the result for the page title, so every detail visit makes two identical requests.
candidates.evidence: A.3: 'Data critical for rendering a page must be fetched via the route's loader function rather than loading it inside the component body.' Loader line 124 calls context.trpcClient?.network.networks.getById.query; line 149 calls trpcReact.network.networks.getById.useQuery with the same input.

candidates.claim: A 401 is handled inline: NetworkLoadError renders an error message ('The session has expired...') in the page instead of redirecting to Sign-in. 403 also renders a plain error page without the page-level info Message explaining the lack of access.
candidates.evidence: B.6 Reject: 'a 401/403 handled inline instead of via redirect / page-level info Message'. Lines 63-66 map FORBIDDEN and UNAUTHORIZED to error descriptions in RouteIdLevelDefaultError.

candidates.claim: The UNAUTHORIZED copy says 'Log in again to continue.' The UX writing rule requires 'Sign in', and the recommended 401 copy is 'Authentication failed. Verify your credentials and try again.'
candidates.evidence: Quick Reject: 'String using ... "Sign In"/"Log in" (use "Sign in")'. B.19: '"Sign in", not "Sign In" or "Log in"'.

candidates.claim: A raw <button> is used for the 'Try Again' action in the subnets error state, where Juno's Button exists. It has no Juno styling or variant.
candidates.evidence: B.1 Reject: 'any PR that introduces a plain <table>, <input>, <select>, or <button> where a Juno equivalent exists.' Line 69: action={<button onClick={() => refetch()}>{t`Try Again`}</button>}. Quick Reject: 'Raw HTML element (<div>, <table>, <button>) where a Juno component exists'.

candidates.claim: The active detail tab is held in useState instead of the URL search params, so the Subnets tab is not shareable and is lost on refresh.
candidates.evidence: B.9: 'All persistent UI state must live in URL search params' with 'Active tab | tab'; 'Reject any useState for state that should survive a page refresh or be shareable via URL.' Line 109: const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState<NetworkDetailsTab>("overview"). Quick Reject: 'URL-worthy state held in useState instead of search params'.

candidates.claim: The row action menu uses <PopupMenu> without a PopupMenuToggle trigger (default toggle), contrary to the required pattern <PopupMenuToggle as="div"><Button icon="moreVert" /></PopupMenuToggle>.
candidates.evidence: Quick Reject: 'PopupMenu without PopupMenuToggle as trigger'; B.14: 'Context menus must use <PopupMenuToggle as="div"><Button icon="moreVert" /></PopupMenuToggle> as the trigger.' Lines 56-60 render <PopupMenu><PopupMenuOptions>...</PopupMenuOptions></PopupMenu> with no PopupMenuToggle; PopupMenuToggle is not imported.

candidates.claim: Network status is rendered as plain text in the list (and detail Overview) instead of a Badge status indicator.
candidates.evidence: B.1: 'Status indicators | Badge'. Line 43: <DataGridCell>{network.status}</DataGridCell>; NetworkDetailsView.tsx:116 value: network.status.

candidates.claim: Admin state is shown as 'UP' / 'DOWN', all-caps strings, which the UX writing rule forbids.
candidates.evidence: Quick Reject: 'String using ... all-caps'; B.19: 'Never all-caps (ever)'. Line 46: network.admin_state_up ? t`UP` : t`DOWN`; same in NetworkDetailsView.tsx:117.

candidates.claim: The label 'Created At' and 'Updated At' capitalise the short preposition 'At', which title-case rules require lowercase.
candidates.evidence: B.19: 'Lowercase ... short prepositions (max 5 letters: at, by, for, in, of, on, to, up...)'. Lines 132-133: t`Created At`, t`Updated At`.

candidates.claim: NetworkListContainer mirrors the currentPage prop into inputPage state through a useEffect. This synchronisation can be handled during render or by keying, and costs an extra render on every page change.
candidates.evidence: A.1: 'Critically evaluate every useEffect hook. Flag synchronizations, computed states ... that can be handled during rendering'. Lines 36-38: useEffect(() => { setInputPage(currentPage.toString()) }, [currentPage]).

candidates.claim: A useEffect corrects an out-of-range page by calling onPageChange(1). This is derived state: safePage is already clamped during render, so the effect only exists to rewrite the URL.
candidates.evidence: A.1: 'Flag synchronizations, computed states, or event-driven triggers ... that can be handled during rendering or inside event handlers'. Lines 97-99: useEffect(() => { if (!isStale && currentPage > totalPages) onPageChange(1) }, ...).

error variant used for a destructive action (should be danger), or vice versa

UI control shown before permissions are resolved (not fail-closed)

toast.success/error with inline string instead of *ToastNotifications
toast.error used for a persistent/actionable error
<Message> variant conflicting with the modal's primary button variant

Destructive modal with alarmist/vague title
PopupMenu without PopupMenuToggle as trigger
"Delete" action not last / missing divider
URL-worthy state held in useState instead of search params
